ProfileBlurbs.SourceTitle: BOYS' PREP BASKETBALL / 10 PLAYERS TO WATCH - WIDE OPEN PARITY SHOULD DOMINATE HIGH SCHOOL BOYS' BASKETBALL IN THE CITY THIS SEASON AS PERENNIAL POWERS LOOK TO MAKE UP FOR KEY LOSSES.
ProfileBlurbs.Headline: Patrick Burns - 2002 Boys' Prep Basketball Player to Watch
ProfileBlurbs.Text: The Savannah Morning News listed Burns among its 10 boys' prep basketball players to watch for the 2002-03 season. The preview described him as a 6-foot-1, 170-pound senior forward and noted that he had dominated his competition a year earlier by posting 14 straight double-doubles.

ProfileBlurbs.Headline: Athlete Spotlight: Davy Clay
ProfileBlurbs.ImageAlt: Savannah Morning News Athlete Spotlight clipping for Davy Clay from Jan. 23, 2004
ProfileBlurbs.Text: The Saints point guard averaged an unusual double-double in points and steals, scoring 12.5 points per game while leading the Coastal Empire with 10.5 steals per game. The January 23, 2004 Savannah Morning News spotlight also noted that Clay, a 5-foot-8, 135-pound senior, led the area in assists at 7.4 per game.
ProfileBlurbs.Quote: Steals are all about being in the right spot at the right time and anticipating passes. I just read people's eyes. And with my size, they always overlook me. Always.

ProfileBlurbs.SourceTitle: TEAM OF SIX CARRIED SAINTS TO STATE TITLE
ProfileBlurbs.Headline: Meghan Lowe, Sr. - SCISA Class AA champion and all-star
ProfileBlurbs.Text: Lowe was the lone senior and only upperclassman on St. Andrew's six-player varsity team, earned a SCISA all-star selection, and helped lead the Saints to the program's first girls basketball state championship.

ProfileBlurbs.SourceTitle: COASTAL EMPIRE VOLLEYBALL PLAYER OF THE YEAR / CHRISSY BARBEE, ST. VINCENT'S, SR. - BARBEE SETS A GOOD EXAMPLE FOR ST. VINCENT'S THE SAINTS SETTER HELPED LEAD HER TEAM TO THEIR FIRST CLASS AAAAA STATE CHAMPIONSHIP
ProfileBlurbs.Headline: Mary Wilkowski, Fr. - 2003 Coastal Empire Volleyball Second Team
ProfileBlurbs.Text: The freshman amazed her coaches with her ability to elevate her game during the season. She finished with 175 kills in 22 matches.

ProfileBlurbs.SourceTitle: COASTAL EMPIRE VOLLEYBALL PLAYER OF THE YEAR / CHRISSY BARBEE, ST. VINCENT'S, SR. - BARBEE SETS A GOOD EXAMPLE FOR ST. VINCENT'S THE SAINTS SETTER HELPED LEAD HER TEAM TO THEIR FIRST CLASS AAAAA STATE CHAMPIONSHIP
ProfileBlurbs.Headline: Carie Bugos, Sr., Setter - 2003 Coastal Empire Volleyball Second Team
ProfileBlurbs.Text: Bugos provided leadership and maturity for the young team. She guided them through their 19-3 season with 195 assists and 145 service points in the 22 matches.

ProfileBlurbs.SourceTitle: COASTAL EMPIRE VOLLEYBALL PLAYER OF THE YEAR / CHRISSY BARBEE, ST. VINCENT'S, SR. - BARBEE SETS A GOOD EXAMPLE FOR ST. VINCENT'S THE SAINTS SETTER HELPED LEAD HER TEAM TO THEIR FIRST CLASS AAAAA STATE CHAMPIONSHIP
ProfileBlurbs.Headline: Becca Cooper, Sr., Middle hitter - 2003 Coastal Empire Volleyball First Team
ProfileBlurbs.Text: Cooper, named to the SCISA AA All-State team, led by example as the strongest hitter on the Saints' court. Her talent made younger players on the St. Andrew's team step up their own performance. St. Andrew's won the SCISA Region IIAA championship (10-0), and finished 19-3 overall and the SCISA AA State championship runner up.
